cues.zh: 在上一期视频中，我们聊了加拿大的城际列车服务 VIA Rail，
cues.en: In the previous video, we talked about VIA Rail, the intercity train service in Canada,

cues.zh: 以及为什么坐火车很难比自己开车更划算。
cues.en: and why it’s really hard to justify taking the train instead of driving.

cues.zh: 今年夏天我又坐了一次 VIA Rail，虽然他们没要求给我行李称重，
cues.en: I took VIA rail again this summer, and though they didn’t ask me to weigh my bags,

cues.zh: 但现在居然也有了值机流程。
cues.en: they do have a check-in process now.

cues.zh: 这让坐火车离坐飞机一样痛苦又近了一步。
cues.en: One step closer to making train travel as painful as airline travel.

cues.zh: 而且由于疫情限制，从伦敦到多伦多的班次
cues.en: And due to corona restrictions, the 7 trains per day from London to Toronto

cues.zh: 已经从每天 7 班减少到了 3 班。错过回多伦多的火车了？
cues.en: has been reduced to 3 trains per day. Did you miss your train to Toronto?

cues.zh: 没关系，下一班……9 小时后再见。
cues.en: That’s OK, there’s another one coming … in 9 hours.

cues.zh: 不过 VIA Rail 就聊到这吧。在这期视频中，
cues.en: But enough about VIA Rail. In this video,

cues.zh: 我想聊聊加拿大最不差劲的重轨列车：GO Transit。
cues.en: I want to talk about the least-terrible heavy rail trains in Canada: GO Transit.

cues.zh: GO Transit 是一种通勤铁路服务，由安大略省政府运营。缩写就是 G.O.。
cues.en: GO Transit is a commuter rail service, run by the Government of Ontario. G.O.

cues.zh: GO（出发）。懂了吧？名字里就写着呢。
cues.en: GO. Get it? It’s right there in the name.

cues.zh: 如今，这些基础设施和列车都由 Metrolinx 运营管理，
cues.en: These days, the infrastructure and trains are managed by Metrolinx,

cues.zh: 它是负责大多伦多地区区域交通的政府机构。
cues.en: the government agency responsible for regional travel in the greater Toronto Area.

cues.zh: GO 还运营着一套公交网络，但这些车跑在普通道路上，经常堵在
cues.en: GO also operates a network of buses, but these run on regular roads and routinely get stuck in

cues.zh: 车流里，所以其实没那么有意思。咱们还是聊聊火车吧！
cues.en: traffic so they’re really not that interesting. Let’s talk about trains!

cues.zh: 作为乘客，坐 GO 火车体验很不错。车站干净且维护良好，
cues.en: As a rider, taking the GO train is quite nice. The stations are clean and well maintained,

cues.zh: 列车是双层的，空间宽敞，座椅也很舒适。
cues.en: the trains are two-levels with plenty of space and comfortable seats.

cues.zh: 车费可以用 Presto 卡支付，
cues.en: Trips can be paid for using the Presto card,

cues.zh: 这是安大略省多个城市公共交通使用的一种非接触式公交卡。
cues.en: a contactless payment card used for public transit in several cities in Ontario.

cues.zh: 总的来说，乘坐体验相当不错，肯定比堵在多伦多的车流里强多了。
cues.en: In general, the experience is pretty good and it sure beats driving in Toronto traffic.

cues.zh: 你甚至不用称行李、提前订票，
cues.en: And you don’t even need to weigh your bags, book an advanced ticket,

cues.zh: 也不用排队上车。就像真正的火车一样！
cues.en: or queue to board. It’s like a real train!

cues.zh: 而且有几个GO车站同时也是VIA Rail的车站，
cues.en: And several GO stations are also VIA Rail stations,

cues.zh: 所以理论上你可以换乘其他列车服务。
cues.en: so you can theoretically connect to other train services.

cues.zh: 当然，前提是你刚好赶上VIA决定开行列车的那一个班次。
cues.en: That is, if you happen to be leaving at that one time VIA decides to run a train.

cues.zh: GO做得非常好的一点是，对轮椅使用者的无障碍通行。
cues.en: One thing that GO does very well is accessibility for wheelchair users.

cues.zh: 每个车站都有指定的区域，设有平层上车通道，方便轮椅进入，
cues.en: Every station has a designated area that has level boarding for wheelchair access,

cues.zh: 而且大多数车站都有质量不错的电梯连接。
cues.en: and there are good quality elevator connections at most stations.

cues.zh: 不过让我觉得奇怪的是，他们明明知道怎么建平层上车通道，
cues.en: It is strange to me though, that they know how to build level boarding,

cues.zh: 却只在这一节无障碍车厢这么做。为什么不在整个站台都这样呢？
cues.en: but only do it at this one accessibility car. Why not along the whole platform?

cues.zh: 但除了台阶式上车之外，有一件事在我试图
cues.en: But beyond the step-up boarding, one thing that really annoyed me when trying to take

cues.zh: 带自行车上火车时真的很烦人，就是门口中间的那根横杆，在
cues.en: a bicycle on the train, is this bar in the middle of the doorway, that gets in the

cues.zh: 推自行车上车时会挡路。然而在一些车门上，包括那些
cues.en: way when trying to board with a bicycle. Yet on some doors, including doors that

cues.zh: 不允许自行车通过的门，却没有那根横杆。为什么？为什么Metrolinx？你们为什么要这样对我们？
cues.en: don’t allow bicycles, they don’t have that bar. Why? Why Metrolinx? Why do you do that to us?

cues.zh: GO Transit 的历史与美国的通勤铁路非常相似。
cues.en: The history of GO Transit is similar to commuter rail in the US.

cues.zh: 二战后，美加两国的城市大力补贴汽车基础设施，
cues.en: After the second world war, US and Canadian cities heavily subsidized car infrastructure,

cues.zh: 根本不在乎这会让客运铁路破产，当时客运铁路被视为过时的产物。
cues.en: and didn’t care that they were bankrupting passenger rail, which was seen as obsolete.

cues.zh: 但到了 1960 年代，至少在主要大城市，人们已经很清楚
cues.en: But by the 1960s, it was pretty clear, in major cities at least,

cues.zh: 这样做是个糟糕的决定，因为根本没有足够的空间容纳所有汽车。
cues.en: that this was a bad idea, because there wasn’t enough room for all the cars.

cues.zh: 因此，像 GO Train 这样的通勤铁路线应运而生，只为一个目的：
cues.en: So commuter rail lines, like the GO Train, were created for one purpose:

cues.zh: 减少早晚高峰期间道路上的郊区通勤车辆。
cues.en: to reduce the number of suburban commuters on the roads during rush hour.

cues.zh: 按这个指标来看，GO Train 取得了巨大的成功。
cues.en: By that metric, the GO Train is a huge success.

cues.zh: 对于住在郊区但在多伦多市中心上班的人来说，67% 的人选择乘坐 GO Train，
cues.en: For people who live in the suburbs, but work in downtown Toronto, 67% take the GO Train,

cues.zh: 而自己开车或拼车的人只有 20%。这让路上少了很多车。
cues.en: while only 20% go by car as a driver or passenger. That’s a lot of cars taken off the road.

cues.zh: 遗憾的是，虽然通勤铁路在服务郊区
cues.en: Unfortunately, while commuter rail does a good job of servicing suburban

cues.zh: 朝九晚五去市中心上班的通勤者方面做得不错，但对其他类型的出行几乎毫无用处。
cues.en: 9 to 5 commuters who work downtown, it is almost useless for any other kind of trip.

cues.zh: 例如，对于那些在大多伦多市中心以外任何地方工作的郊区居民来说，
cues.en: For example, the graph for suburbanites who work anywhere other than downtown Toronto

cues.zh: 出行方式图是这样的。近90%的人开车，
cues.en: looks like this. With almost 90% of people going by car,

cues.zh: 只有1%的人乘坐GO Train。所以按这个标准，GO Train是个彻底的失败。
cues.en: and only 1% who take the GO Train. So by this metric, the GO Train is a colossal failure.

cues.zh: 通勤铁路只是为了把郊区通勤者送到市中心而建的，所以如果你想
cues.en: Commuter rail is only built to bring suburban commuters downtown, so if you want to travel

cues.zh: 从一个郊区车站去另一个郊区车站，就得绕道市中心。
cues.en: from one suburban station to another suburban station, you need to travel via downtown.

cues.zh: 但这样的行程根本不可能实现，因为像这样的时刻表很常见：
cues.en: But this trip wouldn’t be possible anyway, as it’s common to see schedules like this:

cues.zh: 早上四趟车出去，然后这四趟车下午再回来。
cues.en: four trains out in the morning, then those four trains come back in the afternoon.

cues.zh: 想在这些时间段之外出行，或是反方向出行？那就没办法了。
cues.en: Want to travel outside these times, or in the opposite direction? Too bad.

cues.zh: 听到这里的欧洲观众可能会问：大费周章建起整套重轨网络，
cues.en: My European viewers hearing this might ask, isn’t building an entire heavy rail network,

cues.zh: 采购并维护列车车辆，还要给列车和车站配备工作人员，
cues.en: buying and maintaining rolling stock, and staffing the trains and stations,

cues.zh: 结果一天就跑这么几趟车，岂不是巨大的浪费？对此我想说……没错，确实如此。
cues.en: a huge waste of money to run just a few trains per day? And to that I say … yes. Yes it is.

cues.zh: 这些列车整天就停在这里无所事事，白白霸占着
cues.en: These trains sit here all day, doing nothing, and taking up some of the

cues.zh: 整个国家地价最昂贵的地段，仅仅是为了准备好
cues.en: most valuable real estate in the entire country, just so that they’re ready for

cues.zh: 在下午把住在郊区的人送回他们的私家车旁。简直不可理喻。
cues.en: the afternoon when they’ll be used to take suburbanites back to their cars. Insane.

cues.zh: 像 GO Transit 这样的系统，我更愿意称之为“依赖汽车的公交”。
cues.en: Systems like GO Transit are what I like to call “car-dependent transit.”

cues.zh: 也就是说，这种公交只有在你本来就开车的情况下才管用，或者说才最好用。
cues.en: That is, transit that only works, or at least, works best, if you’re already driving.

cues.zh: “停车换乘”这个概念本身没什么问题，
cues.en: There’s nothing inherently wrong with the concept of a “park and ride”,

cues.zh: 但当你的整个铁路网全是“停车换乘”，而且只在高峰时段管用，
cues.en: but when your entire rail network is nothing but “park and rides” that only work at rush hour,

cues.zh: 那就是一个非常失能的公共交通系统。
cues.en: that’s a very dysfunctional transit system.

cues.zh: 通勤铁路的支持者会辩称，这些系统是必要的，否则城市
cues.en: Proponents of commuter rail will argue that it’s necessary to have these systems, otherwise urban

cues.zh: 市中心就会被郊区的汽车淹没。这当然是一种极其以汽车为中心的
cues.en: city centres will be flooded with cars from the suburbs. This is an incredibly car-centric view

cues.zh: 世界观，但也像是对公共交通的黑帮式威胁。
cues.en: of the world, of course, but it’s also like a mafia threat approach to public transit.

cues.zh: 你这城市……呃……不错啊。要是有些郊区居民开车进来，那就可惜了。
cues.en: Nice … uh … city ya got there. Shame if some suburbanites were to drive into it.

cues.zh: 我觉得通勤铁路的存在，恰恰凸显了汽车基础设施有多么
cues.en: I think the existence of commuter rail really highlights just how horrendously

cues.zh: 昂贵得可怕。以至于早在 1960 年代，
cues.en: expensive car infrastructure is. That, even as far back as the 1960s,

cues.zh: 人们就认为，建一个高度补贴、平行的铁路网，
cues.en: it was considered cheaper to build a heavily-subsidized parallel rail network,

cues.zh: 每天只用几个小时，也比扩建公路网更便宜。
cues.en: that was only used for a few hours per day, rather than to expand the highway network.

cues.zh: 这本该是一个巨大、闪烁的警告信号，提醒人们汽车基础设施难以为继，
cues.en: This should have been a giant flashing warning sign that car infrastructure was not sustainable,

cues.zh: 早在 Strong Towns 发现汽车基础设施正在让美国城市破产之前。
cues.en: long before Strong Towns discovered that it was bankrupting American cities.

cues.zh: 2000 年代初我住在多伦多市中心时，GO 火车总让我很恼火。
cues.en: When I was living in downtown Toronto in the early 2000s, the GO Train always frustrated me.

cues.zh: 这里明明有一张覆盖广泛的铁路网，
cues.en: Here was this extensive rail network,

cues.zh: 我住处附近还有一座大站，可对我来说却完全派不上用场。
cues.en: with a major station not far from where I lived. But it was totally useless to me.

cues.zh: 比如有一次，星期天我去圭尔夫参加朋友的派对，
cues.en: For example, I once went to a friend’s party in Guelph on a Sunday,

cues.zh: 想坐 GO 火车回家，因为我爱火车，也爱自找麻烦。
cues.en: and wanted to take the GO Train home because I’m a train-loving masochist.

cues.zh: 当然，通勤列车周末不开，所以我只好在车站附近住一晚，
cues.en: Of course, since commuter trains don’t run on the weekend, I had to get a hotel by the station,

cues.zh: 星期一一早再搭火车回多伦多。
cues.en: and catch the early morning train back to Toronto on Monday.

cues.zh: 但用通勤铁路去非通勤目的地，最大的问题是，
cues.en: But the biggest problem with using commuter rail for non-commuting trips

cues.zh: 大多数火车站都建在郊区的荒凉地带，专为开车的人设计，
cues.en: is that most train stations are in suburban wastelands. They are designed for drivers,

cues.zh: 所以每座郊区 GO 火车站周围都被巨大的停车场包围。
cues.en: which means every suburban GO Train station is surrounded by massive parking lots.

cues.zh: 所以哪怕你想在非通勤时段去郊区，
cues.en: So even if you wanted to go to the suburbs outside of commuting hours,

cues.zh: 又能去哪儿呢？没有车，你寸步难行。
cues.en: where would you go? You’re completely stranded without a car.

cues.zh: 这真的是紧邻
cues.en: Is this really the best use of the land next to

cues.zh: 一座连接加拿大最大城市的主要火车站的土地的最佳用途吗？
cues.en: a major rail station connected to the largest city in Canada?

cues.zh: 事实上，GO Transit是整个安大略省最大的停车场提供者。
cues.en: In fact, GO Transit is the single largest parking provider in the entire province of Ontario.

cues.zh: 比多伦多停车管理局还大，也比任何私营停车场运营商都大。
cues.en: Bigger than the Toronto Parking Authority, and bigger than any private parking garage operator.

cues.zh: 然而他们7万个停车位中几乎全部
cues.en: And yet almost all of their 70,000 parking spots

cues.zh: 都是免费使用的。完全由安大略省的纳税人补贴。
cues.en: are free to use. Completely subsidized by the taxpayers of Ontario.

cues.zh: 这又是郊区司机被高产的城市场所补贴的一种方式。
cues.en: Yet another way that suburbanite drivers are being subsidized by productive urban places.

cues.zh: 每个开车到GO车站、免费停车、再坐火车的人，都在享受补贴。
cues.en: Every person who drives to a GO Station, parks for free, and takes the train, is enjoying a subsidy.

cues.zh: 步行或骑自行车去车站的人，买票没有折扣，
cues.en: There’s no discount on ticket prices for those who walk, or for those who cycle to the station,

cues.zh: 所以他们建了这样一套系统，鼓励人们开车去坐火车。
cues.en: so they’ve built a system that provides financial incentive to drive to the train.

cues.zh: 多伦多市中心有几个车站没有停车场。
cues.en: There are a few stations around downtown Toronto that do not have parking.

cues.zh: 而有些郊区车站可以付费预订车位，确保每天早上到站时
cues.en: And at some suburban stations it’s possible to pay for a reserved parking space to ensure a spot is

cues.zh: 都有车位。不过绝大多数停车位都是免费的。
cues.en: available for you at the station each morning. But the vast majority of parking is free.

cues.zh: 停车位最多的车站是 Pickering GO，
cues.en: The station with the most parking spaces is Pickering GO,

cues.zh: 那里有这样一大片地面停车场，
cues.en: where they have this surface parking lot,

cues.zh: 还有这座巨大的停车楼。要是还不够，
cues.en: this giant parking garage, and in case that’s not enough,

cues.zh: 铁轨另一侧还有一座停车楼，
cues.en: there’s another parking garage on the other side of the tracks,

cues.zh: 要去那里，得通过这座横跨高速公路的大型人行天桥。
cues.en: which requires this huge pedestrian overpass to cross the freeway.

cues.zh: 至少你还能走这座人行天桥去附近的商场，所以
cues.en: At least you can also use this pedestrian overpass to get to a nearby mall, so

cues.zh: 从这个意义上说，它的步行可达性比大多数郊区车站都好。
cues.en: in that sense, it has better pedestrian access than most suburban stations.

cues.zh: 不过你还是得出站，穿过商场的停车场才能到那儿。
cues.en: Though you still need to go outside and cross the mall parking lot to get there.

cues.zh: 看到这么大的停车楼却完全没有收费闸口，
cues.en: It’s really strange to see parking garages this large

cues.zh: 真是挺奇怪的。因为全都是免费的。
cues.en: without any payment gates at all. Because it’s all free.

cues.zh: Metrolinx 还在每个 GO 车站提供免费自行车停放，
cues.en: Metrolinx also provides free bicycle parking at every GO station,

cues.zh: 既方便那些愿意每天沿着这种“stroad”骑车
cues.en: for both cyclists who are comfortable cycling

cues.zh: 往返车站的骑行者。
cues.en: along stroads like this to get to and from the station each day.

cues.zh: 大多数车站也有公交接驳，适合那些愿意
cues.en: And most stations have access by bus, for those who want to pay for

cues.zh: 同时买公交票和火车票、乐于补贴开车族的人。
cues.en: both a bus ticket and a train ticket, and enjoy subsidizing the people who drive.

cues.zh: Metrolinx 计划把部分停车位改成收费停车，
cues.en: Metrolinx has plans to convert some of their parking spaces to paid parking,

cues.zh: 他们还谈过要把停车场改造成公交导向社区，也就是
cues.en: and they have talked about converting parking lots to Transit Oriented Communities, neighborhoods of

cues.zh: GO 火车站附近的混合用途开发社区。但这些工作的进展很慢。
cues.en: mixed-use development near GO Train stations. But progress on these activities is slow.

cues.zh: 但谢天谢地，希望还没有完全破灭。虽然GO
cues.en: But thankfully, all hope is not lost. While the GO

cues.zh: 列车最初是作为通勤铁路网络建造的，但Metrolinx已经开始
cues.en: Train was originally built as a commuter rail network, Metrolinx has started to

cues.zh: 意识到，一个广泛的列车网络对其他出行也同样有用。
cues.en: realize that an extensive train network could be useful for other trips as well.

cues.en: For example, the Lakeshore West line has had all-day train service every 30 minutes

cues.en: since 2013. We’ve used this many times to visit friends in the suburbs.

cues.zh: 是的，我承认。我们在郊区有朋友。我肯定会因此被“取消”的
cues.en: Yes, I admit it. We have friends in the suburbs. I’m going to get so cancelled for this

cues.en: But the biggest improvement will come with the Go Expansion Project, where Metrolinx plans to

cues.zh: 将几条GO Transit线路电气化，在几条线路上提供每15分钟或更优的班次，
cues.en: electrify several GO Transit lines, run service every 15 minutes or better on several lines,

cues.zh: 并将服务从每周1500趟列车增加到每周超过6000趟列车。
cues.en: and increase service from 1500 trains per week to over 6 thousand trains per week.

cues.zh: 这从根本上改变了多伦多地区的铁路出行，
cues.en: This will fundamentally change rail travel in the Toronto area,

cues.zh: 我真的非常期待。
cues.en: and I’m really looking forward to it.

cues.zh: 不过，尽管 GO Transit 的未来值得期待，Metrolinx

cues.zh: 却并没有停止让自己在“汽车依赖”的泥潭里越陷越深。
cues.en: hasn’t exactly stopped digging a deeper hole of car-dependency that they’ll need to climb out of.

cues.zh: GO Train 网络中最新的 Bloomington GO 车站，
cues.en: The newest station on the GO Train network, Bloomington GO,

cues.zh: 几个月前才刚刚启用，它简直就是“汽车依赖型公交”的典型代表。
cues.en: opened only a few months ago, and it is the pinnacle of car-dependent transit.

cues.zh: Bloomington GO 坐落在一片荒无人烟的地方。一点都不夸张。
cues.en: Bloomington GO is in the middle of nowhere. Literally.

cues.zh: 它位于“绿化带”内，这是大多伦多地区的一块受保护绿地兼城市增长边界，
cues.en: It’s in the “green belt”, a protected greenspace and urban growth boundary for

cues.zh: 从理论上讲，这里本不应该有任何新的开发项目。
cues.en: the Greater Toronto Area which is theoretically not supposed to have any new development in it.

cues.zh: 这个火车站规模非常庞大。它拥有一个巨大的地面停车场，
cues.en: This train station is absolutely massive. It has a large surface parking lot,

cues.zh: 还设有供车辆即停即走的送客区。
cues.en: with a “kiss and ride” area for people being dropped off by car.

cues.zh: 车站坐落在一条乡村公路旁，紧邻一条主要的高速公路。
cues.en: The station is off of a rural highway next to a major freeway.

cues.zh: 每个人都只能开车去那里。
cues.en: Everybody is going to have to drive there.

cues.zh: 然而，通往车站的道路边
cues.en: And yet, it has this painted bicycle gutter along the access

cues.zh: 却画着这种敷衍的自行车道。难以置信的是，这么大一座从零建起的车站，
cues.en: road to the station. It’s crazy that this huge station was built from scratch,

cues.zh: 竟然觉得画条白线就算是合格的自行车道了。
cues.en: and yet this painted line was considered acceptable access by bicycle.

cues.zh: 这几乎可以肯定只是为了应付某些所谓的“可持续”、“绿色
cues.en: This was almost certainly just a checklist item for some kind of “sustainable” “active

cues.zh: 出行”指标而勾选的打勾项。根本不会有人去用这种敷衍的自行车道。
cues.en: transportation” requirements. Nobody will ever use this painted bicycle gutter.

cues.en: Speaking of checklists, the Bloomington GO station building meets the sustainable

cues.zh: LEED 金级认证的可持续建筑标准，
cues.en: building requirements to be LEED Gold certified,

cues.zh: 因为配备了太阳能电池板、LED 灯和节水洁具等环保设施。
cues.en: because of environmentally friendly features like solar panels, LED lights, and low-flow plumbing.

cues.zh: 然而，超过90%的面积都用于为上千辆机动车提供免费停车位。
cues.en: And yet over 90% of the area is dedicated to free parking for over a thousand motor vehicles.

cues.zh: 我多年来一直这么说，但我认为，在依赖汽车的地方，建筑根本不应获得LEED认证。
cues.en: I’ve been saying this for years, but I think it should be impossible to get LEED certification

cues.zh: 因为这会是一个
cues.en: for buildings in car-dependent places. Because it would be an

cues.zh: 建造一个小巧紧凑的车站，环保程度要高出一个数量级，
cues.en: order of magnitude more environmentally friendly to build a small, compact station,

cues.zh: 周围是步行可达的混合用途社区。
cues.en: surrounded by mixed-use neighborhoods within walking distance.

cues.zh: 结果我们却得到了这座汽车依赖的大教堂。
cues.en: Instead, we get this cathedral of car dependency.

cues.zh: 当然，即便有这样的规定，
cues.en: Of course, even with a rule like that,

cues.zh: 这栋建筑依然能获得 LEED 认证，因为它就在火车站旁。唉。
cues.en: this building would still be LEED certified because it’s at a train station. Sigh.

cues.zh: 但这一切……能停上千辆车的停车场，
cues.en: But all of this … the parking for over a thousand cars,

cues.zh: 进出的道路、透水铺装，
cues.en: the roads in and out, the water-permeable pavers,

cues.zh: 清单式的自行车棚，还有超过 8200 万美元的总造价，
cues.en: the checklist bike shed, And a total cost of over $82 million dollars,

cues.zh: 都是为了支持这一个月台，它只服务 4 趟列车，而且只在高峰时段。
cues.en: Is here to support this one train platform that services 4 trains, and only at rush hour.

cues.zh: 一个站台。
cues.en: One platform.

cues.zh: 票价永远不可能收回这笔投资。
cues.en: The ticket prices will never be able to recoup this investment.

cues.zh: 这只是给依赖汽车的郊区居民提供的又一笔巨额补贴。
cues.en: It’s just one more massive subsidy provided to car-dependent suburbanites.

cues.zh: 这简直像是从 20 世纪 60 年代的交通规划里照搬出来的。
cues.en: This is something right out of 1960s travel planning.

cues.zh: 这居然是 2021 年建成的，真让我恼火。而且这座车站将永远依赖汽车，
cues.en: It genuinely annoys me that this was built in 2021. And this will forever be a car-dependent

cues.zh: 因为绿化带内不允许新建开发项目。
cues.en: station because new development isn’t supposed to be built in the Greenbelt.

cues.zh: 我最不满依赖汽车的交通开发之处，在于它完全忽视了公共交通最大的好处。
cues.en: My biggest issue with car-dependent transit development is that it completely ignores the

cues.zh: 没错，公共交通的作用是把人们送到想去的地方，
cues.en: biggest benefit of public transit. Yes, transit is meant to bring people to where they want to go,

cues.zh: 但它真正的价值，是成为催化剂，帮助建成那些人们想去的地方。
cues.en: but it’s actually most useful by being a catalyst to build the places where people want to go.

cues.zh: 美国和加拿大都是依托铁路发展起来的。
cues.en: Both the US and Canada were built on their railroads.

cues.zh: 19世纪时，大多数铁路公司都设立了高利润的
cues.en: In the 19th century, most railroads established profitable

cues.zh: 土地部门，用来出售因修建铁路而升值的土地。
cues.en: land departments that would sell the land made valuable by the railroad they built.

cues.zh: 公共交通在创造区域财富方面，拥有令人难以置信的能力。
cues.en: Public transit has an unbelievable ability to build wealth in places.

cues.zh: 它能让一个地方真正值得一去。
cues.en: To make places worth going to.

cues.zh: 但通勤铁路却把这些红利当垃圾一样扔掉了，
cues.en: But commuter rail tosses those benefits in the garbage,

cues.zh: 在为汽车打造的世界里，沦为了无足轻重的边缘配角。
cues.en: relegating transit to a background activity in a world designed for cars.

cues.zh: 它唯一真正的好处，不过是让你不用堵在路上，
cues.en: Where the only real benefit provided is that you’re not driving in traffic, and

cues.zh: 或者顶多让你不用付市中心的停车费。
cues.en: maybe, that you don’t need to pay for parking downtown.

cues.zh: 对公共交通来说，这个角色真的很可悲，
cues.en: This is a really sad role for transit, which has the

cues.zh: 如果规划得当，它本应是城市最大的财富创造引擎。
cues.en: potential to be the largest wealth-creation opportunity for cities, if done correctly.

cues.zh: Bloomington GO 以及类似的车站确实能吸引开发，
cues.en: Bloomington GO, and stations like it, will attract development,

cues.zh: 但绝不是我们真正想要或需要的开发模式。
cues.en: but not the development we actually want or need.

cues.zh: 比如，开车不远，我就看到了这个正在建设的社区，它
cues.en: For example, a short drive away I came across this neighbourhood under construction, which

cues.zh: 是一个远郊社区：一个依赖汽车、不依附于任何城市的郊区开发项目。它只是一个孤立的
cues.en: is an exurb: a car-dependent suburban development not attached to any city. It’s just a disconnected

cues.zh: 社区，位于荒郊野外，没有任何环境背景，也不靠近任何地方。
cues.en: neighborhood in the middle of nowhere, devoid of any context, and nowhere near anything.

cues.zh: 现在，这个社区的建设并不仅仅是因为附近有一个GO车站，
cues.en: Now, this neighbourhood isn’t being built just because there’s a GO station nearby,

cues.zh: 但开发商的市场宣传材料却把它列为社区的一大优势，
cues.en: but it’s listed as a benefit of the neighbourhood on the builder’s marketing material,

cues.zh: 而这正是依赖汽车的公共交通所鼓励的那种开发模式。
cues.en: and this is the kind of development that’s encouraged by car-dependent transit.

cues.zh: GO Transit的未来无疑充满希望。
cues.en: The future of GO Transit is definitely promising.

cues.zh: 电气化和更多全天候服务肯定会带来改变。
cues.en: Electrification and more all-day service will definitely make a difference.

cues.zh: 但只要GO Transit网络主要被设计成一种往返市中心的
cues.en: But as long as the GO Transit network is designed primarily as a way of getting

cues.zh: 交通方式，只要郊区车站继续容纳的是汽车，
cues.en: to and from downtown, and as long as the suburban stations continue to house cars,

cues.zh: 而不是人，它就永远只有一个结局：巨大的潜力被白白浪费。
cues.en: instead of people, it will always be one thing: a colossal wasted potential.
